column46:
#resources with labels ÷ #triples is almost always close to 0, because a dataset has many more triples than resources. With 1,000 resources, all labelled, and 20,000 triples, the score is −1 + 0.05 = −0.95. Suggested fix: −1 + #resources with labels ÷ #resources

Wrt. to readability, I think the FR is simplyfing the notion of readability. There is indeed work on how to asses the readability or understandability of text or data; e.g. discussed here: https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Lisa-Ehrlinger/publication/333647324_A_Schema_Readability_Metric_for_Automated_Data_Quality_Measurement/links/5cf9410e92851c874c52ea4f/A-Schema-Readability-Metric-for-Automated-Data-Quality-Measurement.pdf

Further, FR is only defined for English. For other languages you need adapted formulas (e.g., Amstad for German, Fernández Huerta for Spanish), or you restrict the dimension to English descriptions and say so.
column67: The dimensions use three ranges ([0, 1], [−1, 0] and [−1, 1]), so a score of 0 means the worst, the best or a neutral result depending on the dimension. As a result, each category's possible range depends on its mix of dimensions (0 to 1 for perceivable, −0.8 to 0.4 for understandable), so category scores can't be interpreted or compared.
column85: I give lower scores to Versioning, Robots.txt and Canonical Identifier for clarity because the key terms are undefined ("standard versioning", accepted identifier schemes) or the description is inaccurate (robots.txt sits at the server root and isn't declared in metadata). Webpage Availability and Broken Metadata Link Rate are clearer, but their scoring functions does not consider tow edge cases: how redirects are handled, how often availability is checked, and what the score is when there are no metadata links.
column94:
WCAG is organized by criteria by principle, not by disability, and both dimensions are text or audio alternatives, which belong in the perceivable category. A separate category for one user group (i.e., visually impaired) would count the same features multiple times and suggest that the framework ignores other groups (deaf, motor-impaired or cognitively impaired users).

Wrt. to the scoring functions: Neither scoring function defines a score for datasets without images or videos (division by zero), and the audio description function divides by all entities instead of by videos, so almost every dataset scores close to −1.
column118: the score is undefined when there are no videos or audio items (division by zero), and none of the functions name the RDF properties they check (e.g., schema:caption, schema:transcript).
